title: Tiny Leader: The Class Poster Project
subtitle: Can you lead your group without bossing everyone around?
description: Your teacher picked YOU to lead the class poster project. Four classmates, four big personalities, one poster. How will you keep everyone working together?
learning_objectives: Understand that a good leader listens before deciding
Practice including different ideas even when you disagree
Learn that adapting your plan when something goes wrong is a sign of strength
reflection_prompt: What was the hardest part of being the leader? What would you do differently next time?

scenes.title: You Are the Leader
scenes.narration: Ms Priya announces: 'The poster about Our Community is due Friday. I am putting you in charge.' Your group: Dia who loves art, Sam who only wants to do the writing, Karan who keeps joking around, and Meera who is very quiet.

choices.label: Assign roles yourself: art, writing, border, research
Ask everyone what they would like to do
Start making the poster yourself — it is faster

scenes.narrative: Ms Priya announces: 'The poster about Our Community is due Friday. I am putting you in charge.' Your group: Dia who loves art, Sam who only wants to do the writing, Karan who keeps joking around, and Meera who is very quiet.

scenes.narration: Sam refuses to do the border. 'I said I want to write.' Karan draws a funny face on the poster that was meant to be blank space.

choices.label: Stay calm and swap their roles — Sam writes, Karan draws the border properly
Tell Karan off loudly in front of everyone

scenes.narrative: Sam refuses to do the border. 'I said I want to write.' Karan draws a funny face on the poster that was meant to be blank space.

scenes.narration: Dia wants art, Sam wants writing, Karan wants to do 'something fun', Meera shrugs. You spot a gap — research and border still need someone.

choices.label: Gently ask Meera what she thinks she might like
Take research yourself and give border to Karan

scenes.narrative: Dia wants art, Sam wants writing, Karan wants to do 'something fun', Meera shrugs. You spot a gap — research and border still need someone.

scenes.narration: After ten minutes you are tired and the poster looks half empty. Your group is sitting around doing nothing.

choices.label: Stop and ask for help — 'I cannot do this alone'
Keep going — you can do it

scenes.narrative: After ten minutes you are tired and the poster looks half empty. Your group is sitting around doing nothing.

scenes.narration: Meera whispers that she is good at finding information. She prints three great facts no one else knew. The poster earns a gold star.
scenes.outcome_summary: You listened and found a hidden talent. The best leaders do not just manage tasks — they discover strengths.
scenes.narrative: Meera whispers that she is good at finding information. She prints three great facts no one else knew. The poster earns a gold star.

scenes.narration: The poster gets done on time. It is not perfect, but everyone did something. Ms Priya says, 'Good teamwork, everyone.'
scenes.outcome_summary: You kept the team moving by being flexible. That is real leadership.
scenes.narrative: The poster gets done on time. It is not perfect, but everyone did something. Ms Priya says, 'Good teamwork, everyone.'

scenes.narration: The group falls apart. The poster is half finished when the bell rings. Ms Priya gives you extra time but looks disappointed.
scenes.outcome_summary: Even leaders make mistakes. The important thing is to notice what went wrong and try something different next time.
